evals.name: full-inventory-report
evals.prompt: Зроби повний аудит залежностей репозиторію: що на що зав'язано, скільки важить, і що чинити першим.
evals.expected_output: A report in the five fixed sections — Scope, Dependency graph, Size breakdown, Findings & Priorities, Summary — in that order. Scope names all six packages (server, client, reviewer-core, e2e, mcp, evals) with their package managers. The graph is a Mermaid flowchart of packages only, with labelled edges. Findings are grouped under P0/P1/P2/Info with empty tiers stated. Summary is 3-5 ordered actions.
assertions: The report has all five sections with the exact headings Scope, Dependency graph, Size breakdown, Findings & Priorities, Summary, in that order
Scope lists all six package roots — server, client, reviewer-core, e2e, mcp and evals — not only the four modules named in root CLAUDE.md
Scope states the package manager per package and gets it right: pnpm for server, client and evals; npm for reviewer-core, e2e and mcp
The graph is a fenced mermaid flowchart whose nodes are the repo's own packages, with no npm package appearing as a node
Every finding is filed under exactly one of P0, P1, P2 or Info, and tiers with nothing in them are written out as empty rather than omitted
Every finding names a package plus a file path or a package.json field
The Summary is 3-5 concrete actions in priority order, not a restatement of the findings

evals.name: unused-hunt-resists-false-positives
evals.prompt: Здається, у нас накопичилось багато зайвих пакетів. Які залежності можна безпечно видалити?
evals.expected_output: Names the three genuinely unused declarations — @fastify/autoload and testcontainers in server/package.json, tsx in reviewer-core/package.json — and explicitly rules out the look-alikes: typescript (invoked as tsc from scripts), tailwindcss/postcss (loaded by postcss.config.mjs), pino-pretty (a pino transport named by string in server/src/app.ts), @vscode/ripgrep (used for its binary), @types/* (never imported by design). Recommends removal; does not perform it.
assertions: Identifies @fastify/autoload in server/package.json as declared under dependencies and imported nowhere
Identifies testcontainers in server/package.json as unused, and distinguishes it from @testcontainers/postgresql which is actually used
Does NOT claim typescript is unused — recognises it is invoked as the tsc binary from the typecheck script
Does NOT claim pino-pretty is unused — recognises server/src/app.ts names it as a pino transport target by string
Does NOT claim tailwindcss, postcss or @tailwindcss/postcss are unused — recognises postcss.config.mjs references them
Does NOT list @types/* packages as unused, since type packages are consumed by the compiler and never imported
Presents removal as a recommendation for the user to confirm and does not edit any package.json or run any install command

evals.name: cross-package-links-are-not-workspaces
evals.prompt: Поясни, як наші пакети зав'язані один на одного. Малюй схему.
evals.expected_output: Describes tsconfig path aliases as the linking mechanism, never workspaces or workspace:* protocol. Names the real edges: server -> reviewer-core via @devdigest/reviewer-core, reviewer-core -> server and mcp -> server via @devdigest/shared, and the client's vendored mirror of server/src/vendor/shared which no tool reports. Flags reviewer-core/test/run.test.ts reaching into server/src/adapters/mocks.js as a boundary violation.
assertions: States that this is not a workspace — six independent packages with six lockfiles, no root package.json, no hoisting
Never claims the packages are linked by pnpm workspaces, npm workspaces or the workspace:* protocol
Names tsconfig paths as the actual linking mechanism and cites at least one concrete alias such as @devdigest/shared or @devdigest/reviewer-core
Identifies that the canonical shared contracts live inside server/src/vendor/shared and that reviewer-core and mcp both reach into server for them
Mentions client/src/vendor/shared as a hand-maintained mirror rather than an import edge
Flags reviewer-core/test/run.test.ts importing server/src/adapters/mocks.js as a deep import across a package boundary, at P0 or otherwise explicitly called out
Produces a mermaid flowchart whose edges carry the mechanism as a label rather than bare arrows

evals.name: installed-size-is-not-bundle-size
evals.prompt: У нас node_modules роздувся до півтора гігабайта. Що найважче і що з цим робити?
evals.expected_output: Reports installed sizes per package (client ~620 MB, evals ~332 MB, server ~250 MB) and the heaviest packages (next ~153 MB, mermaid ~75 MB, lucide-react ~36 MB, typescript 22.8 MB installed six times). Distinguishes disk cost from browser payload, notes that only client can produce the latter, and does not present a du number as a bundle number. Explains that duplicate installs are the price of having no workspace rather than a fixable hoisting problem.
assertions: Reports installed size per package and identifies client as the heaviest
Explicitly distinguishes installed size on disk from what a user downloads in the browser, and does not present a du measurement as a bundle size
Notes that only client produces browser payload, so weight in server, evals, e2e or mcp costs CI and disk but nothing to a user
Identifies duplicate installs across packages — typescript installed once per package is the clearest case — and quantifies the total
Explains that without a workspace root there is nothing to hoist into, so deduplication is not available as a cheap fix
Does not claim a specific bundle-size improvement it has not measured
